ha, chiefly Vermentino and Cannonau alongside the natives Nasco, Nuragus, Bovale, Carignano, Monica and Malvasia Sarda

observations.unit: qualitative

observations.unit: qualitative

observations.unit: qualitative

ha at Rocca Bernarda, Buttrio and Rosazzo in the Colli Orientali. SOURCE CONFLICT: figures range 35ha, 43ha, 55ha and 65ha depending on the source and date. ALIAS: the estate is Le Vigne di Zamo; the corpus carries the bare family name "Zamo"

ha of vineyard owned by the brothers, planted to Corvina, Rondinella and Molinara. SOURCE CONFLICT: another source gives the farm as about 50ha

observations.unit: year — founded on the initiative of Christian Schrott, a pastor and member of the Austrian parliament; one of the oldest cooperatives in Alto Adige. ALIAS: Kellerei Tramin / Cantina Tramin, both names in use

observations.unit: year — David S. Stare founded the winery by buying and replanting a prune orchard opposite the Dry Creek General Store in Sonoma; his daughter Kim Stare Wallace is president. ALIAS: the estate is Dry Creek Vineyard; Dry Creek Valley is also the AVA name, so the corpus string is doubly loaded
ha — 185 acres of sustainably farmed vineyard in Dry Creek Valley

observations.unit: year — the Sportoletti family have farmed the hills between Assisi and Spello for generations; the brothers Ernesto and Remo turned to wine in the 1970s and released the first bottles under their own label in 1979
ha on the hillsides of Spello and Assisi, all inside the Assisi DOC zone. SOURCE CONFLICT: another source gives about 30ha

observations.value: Assisi DOC and Umbria IGT; Villa Fidelia is the estate's senior label

ha — a nearly 10-acre property of which about 7 acres are planted; a genuinely small Napa holding

observations.value: a Merlot-led Napa house in the Right Bank idiom, part of the Bespoke Collection
observations.unit: qualitative
generations — the brothers Clement and Florian Berthier are the fifth generation and took over in 2013; Florian works the vines, Clement the cellar and sales. ALIAS: also trades as Vignobles Berthier
ha across Coteaux du Giennois and Sancerre, with wines also from Menetou-Salon and Pouilly-Fume

observations.value: organic and minimal-intervention practice in the vineyard; Terre de Silex is the flint-soil Coteaux du Giennois cuvee

ALIAS: Calx is the wine, made by Filippo Cassano, who founded Cantine Polvanera in 2002 at Gioia del Colle in Puglia. The name is Latin for limestone, after the Altopiano delle Murge on which the vines sit. Sold in the US through PortoVino's FUSO project
organic farming, fermentation in steel only and no barrels at all; iron-rich soils over limestone and early picking hold the Primitivo to about 12.5% — the opposite of the rich stereotype

observations.unit: year — the Geoffray family have made wine on Mont Brouilly since 1877; Thivin is the oldest estate on the hill, run today by the fifth generation, Claude and Evelyne Geoffray with their son Claude-Edouard and Sonia
ha, one of the largest holdings on Mont Brouilly — 8.3ha in Cote de Brouilly on the east, south and south-west faces, plus parcels in Brouilly

observations.value: the Cote de Brouilly parcels sit on the volcanic blue andesite of Mont Brouilly, giving wines of violet and peony with bluish reflections — the reference estate of the cru

observations.unit: year — Dimitris Hatzimichalis bought his first 9ha in the Atalanti valley in 1973, choosing the site for the microclimate where the cool air off Parnassus meets the sea air of the Euboean gulf
ha of vineyard planted to both Greek and international varieties

observations.value: run by Dimitris L. Hatzimichalis with his sons Leonidas and Panagiotis; a second estate at Arma joins the Atalanti base

observations.unit: year — founded in the Fteri area of the Mantinia plateau in Arcadia
ha of private vineyard on the high, cool Mantinia plateau. SOURCE CONFLICT: one source gives 24ha in total, probably including contracted parcels

observations.value: a Moschofilero specialist; Fteri is its named-site bottling and the Ekato rose has been reviewed by Jancis Robinson

observations.unit: year — the modern estate dates from 2011, on land historically held by the Ridolfi, a noble Florentine family with considerable holdings in Montalcino
ha under vine within a 35ha property, of which 13.5ha are registered for Brunello

observations.value: the winemaker Gianni Maccari is one of the last pupils of Giulio Gambelli, widely regarded as the greatest Tuscan winemaker of his era

observations.unit: year — Axel Prufer, born in East Germany, has made wine in the Languedoc since 2003. SPELLING: the domaine is "Le Temps des Cerises", singular Le; the corpus carries "Les"

observations.value: named after the revolutionary Paris Commune song "Le Temps des Cerises"; the cuvee Avanti Popolo continues the theme

Cinsault, Grenache, Carignan and Aramon, more recently joined by Merlot and Cabernet in conversion to chemical-free farming; bottled unfined, unfiltered, with no added sulphur. A reference name for glouglou natural reds

observations.unit: ha on terraces about 200m above La Liviniere, between Narbonne and Carcassonne. SOURCE CONFLICT: sources give 34ha, 35ha in one block and 40ha of south-facing hillside at 225-250m. ALIAS: the corpus abbreviates Chateau Sainte-Eulalie

observations.value: Minervois La Liviniere, now recognised as a Cru de Languedoc with its own appellation; La Cantilene is the estate's senior bottling

observations.unit: ha — approx.; sources give 71 to 92ha across Brouilly, Morgon, Fleurie, Beaujolais-Villages and Beaujolais rose and white. Les Roches is an 8ha parcel in the south-west of Brouilly on granitic sand at 400-500m

observations.value: works named parcels including Les Roches in Brouilly and Poncie in Fleurie; farmed to HVE certification, within Domaines Richard

observations.unit: year — the Calabretta family have farmed Etna's indigenous Nerello Mascalese and Nerello Cappuccio since 1900

observations.value: Cala Cala — "gulp, gulp" in Massimiliano Calabretta's words — comes from the younger Nerello vines and is usually blended across vintages; the Vigne Vecchie bottlings come from the oldest parcels

observations.unit: ha of organically farmed vineyard within a 350ha estate — 25ha of Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi in the Classico zone plus 6ha of Montepulciano and Sangiovese for Rosso Piceno

observations.unit: qualitative

Pinot Grigio delle Venezie DOC, from river-valley and mountain-slope sites in the Veneto

observations.unit: qualitative

ha in the heart of Valpolicella

ha across six hills between 450 and 850m, with 12 different soil types and 55 indigenous and international varieties. SOURCE CONFLICT: sources give 500, 550 and nearly 600ha

countries — one of the most widely distributed Albarino producers

bottles/yr, half of it exported
years — the family have been in wine for more than a century in the Colli Orientali del Friuli

observations.unit: year — founded in 1993 in the heart of the Alpilles at Eygalieres, exposed to the Provencal sun and the mistral
ha of Grenache, Syrah, Mourvedre, Rolle, Roussanne and others — ten Mediterranean varieties, seven for rose and red and three for white. SOURCE CONFLICT: one source gives 35ha

observations.unit: qualitative

ha — approx.; sources give 20ha, 24ha and 45ha across many small parcels at Berlou in Saint-Chinian, on schist. DEFECT: the corpus files the region as "France (unspecified)" — the domaine is in the Languedoc

drawn from overlooked California vineyard sites rather than one estate, and released in numbered Lots rather than vintages

observations.unit: USD — approx. average retail; deliberately positioned as an accessible Cabernet by a name known for the opposite

the Falanghina grows in the northernmost part of Campania, in the Massico mountains on the Lazio border, on soils shaped by two volcanoes

observations.unit: year — Fattoria La Valentina was founded on the hills above Spoltore near Pescara in 1990 by the Di Properzio brothers. ALIAS: the estate is La Valentina; the corpus carries the bare "Valentina"

observations.value: all estate vineyards certified organic since 2016; the consulting oenologist Luca D'Attoma has worked with the estate since 1998
Spelt is the first selection of Montepulciano, 18 months in wood; the name is the wheat (farro) that once grew where the winery and Spoltore now stand — Spoltore itself derives from it

observations.unit: year — the Real de Asua brothers Eusebio and Raimundo founded Compania Vinicola del Norte de Espana at Haro in 1879; still controlled by their direct descendants. ha owned across the group, which also holds Vina Real and Vinedos del Contino
bottles/yr — one of the largest quality houses in Rioja

ha in the Friuli Colli Orientali DOC around Buttrio. SOURCE CONFLICT: one source gives 86ha

observations.value: Ronco Broilo is the named cru; the estate also bottles the rare Picolit

observations.unit: year — Michel Chapoutier established the domaine in Alsace in 2006, at Bernardville in the Bas-Rhin

ha on the only strip of blue schist in Alsace — which is what the name means, "schist head" — at 380m facing south to south-east, among the highest vineyards in the region. SOURCE CONFLICT: an early account gives 5ha. The Lieu-dit Fels parcel is 0.8ha

observations.value: organically farmed; Riesling, Gewurztraminer and Sylvaner from named lieux-dits

observations.unit: years — approx.; the chateau was built in the 17th century at La Chapelle-Heulin near Nantes and is regarded as one of the cradles of Muscadet
ha of vineyard plus 5ha of woodland per the estate's own site. SOURCE CONFLICT: other sources give 45ha of vineyard

observations.value: Muscadet Sevre-et-Maine sur lie from Melon de Bourgogne, eight months on fine lees
observations.unit: qualitative

cases/yr, from its own grapes in Reggio Emilia

observations.value: Lambrusco di Sorbara and Grasparossa alongside Malvasia Dolce; Rubigalia is its aromatic low-alcohol Malvasia di Candia sparkler and Oblio a Lambrusco-Cabernet blend

observations.unit: year — established at Leporano in the province of Taranto by the Varvaglione family
ha, producing about 60,000 bottles a year

observations.unit: qualitative

observations.value: created by the Begovic cousins — one from north-eastern Slovenia, the other from the Dalmatian coast, who found their shared lineage in the village of Kozice — with the US importer Vinum, to bring minimal-intervention Croatian wine to America. "Pomalo" means take it easy, no worries

observations.unit: years, on pseudogley soils in the Pannonian basin of Slavonia; hand-picked, destemmed and pressed with minimal skin contact, spontaneous fermentation and four months on fine lees

observations.value: Enrico Marcato Family of Wine is a collection of brands rather than a single estate — a new reading of what northern Veneto can make, including the I Prandi Pinot Noir the corpus carries

observations.unit: year — founded by the French Count Hugues Bernard de la Gatinais and his Sicilian wife Gigi Guarrasi, marrying Sicilian viticulture to French technique. ALIAS: the estate is Tenuta Rapitala; the corpus drops the accent
ha on hills between 300 and 600m running from Camporeale toward Alcamo, of which about 105ha are vine. SOURCE CONFLICT: sources give 175, 176 and 225ha

observations.value: part of Gruppo Italiano Vini; Alto Reale is its Nero d'Avola

observations.unit: ha, chiefly around Castiglione Tinella with smaller parcels at Santo Stefano Belbo, Castagnole delle Lanze and Calosso; the Moscato d'Asti comes from a 22ha estate vineyard at the highest point of Castiglione Tinella. SOURCE CONFLICT: one source gives 46ha

observations.value: Paolo Saracco is among the reference names for Moscato d'Asti, to the point of being called the Moscato king in the trade

observations.unit: years — the domaine in the Reginu valley at Feliceto in the Balagne marked its 120th anniversary; the corpus files it under Calenzana, a neighbouring commune in the same Calvi zone
ha farmed organically and biodynamically. SOURCE CONFLICT: one source gives about 30ha

observations.unit: year — founded in the Isonzo area of Friuli-Venezia Giulia
ha under cultivation in the Isonzo foothills and Collio. SOURCE CONFLICT: sources give 42, 44 and 50ha

observations.unit: years — the castle, originally Vicchio dei Longobardi, is documented from around 1100; Leonardo da Vinci stayed there while working on the Mona Lisa and left a drawing of it among his manuscripts. The Matta family have owned and run it since 1964
ha of vine within a 140ha property on the hill above the Greve valley

observations.unit: year — Francis Ford Coppola reopened the Geyserville estate in July 2010 after buying it in 2006 and renovating for two years; the site had made wine since 1973 as Chateau Souverain. Sold to Delicato Family Wines in 2021
ha — the 88-acre Geyserville property in Alexander Valley, Sonoma County

observations.value: Archimedes is the estate's named Alexander Valley Cabernet vineyard
observations.unit: qualitative

observations.unit: qualitative

observations.unit: year — the Capponi family have held Villa Calcinaia at Montefioralle, on the left bank of the Greve, since 1524; the estate marked its quincentenary in 2024

observations.value: the house that redefined Montepulciano d'Abruzzo as a serious wine; Castello di Semivicoli is its restored baroque palazzo

year — created by Chuck Wagner of Caymus and launched in 1989, starting the California proprietary-white-blend trend. RELATED: the same family appears in the corpus as [[Bonanza]]

observations.unit: year — established by Job Bearsley; the name Taylor, Fladgate & Yeatman was formalised by partnership deed in 1838 between Joseph Taylor, John Fladgate and Morgan Yeatman
ha of vines at Quinta de Vargellas, bought in 1893, within a 191ha property in the wild eastern Douro; prized as a source of the finest ports since the 1820s

observations.unit: year — the Portuguese entrepreneur Bruno da Silva founded the business in London in 1798; it became Silva & Cosens, merged with Dow & Co. in 1877 and took the Dow's name. Andrew James Symington became a partner in 1912 and the Symingtons sole owners in 1961

known for the driest style among the classic vintage Port houses
observations.unit: qualitative
year — founded by Dutch settlers, the family line running from Franciscus Marius van der Niepoort; still family-owned across five generations

ha of organically farmed land split between Quinta de Napoles and Quinta do Carril. SOURCE CONFLICT: another source gives over 80ha. Napoles, bought in 1987 above the Tedo in Cima Corgo, carries about 30ha

observations.unit: year — Don Jose Ruiz-Berdejo began working the family estate Nuestra Senora de la Esperanza outside Jerez in 1896. The house was an almacenista until 1945, when it began bottling its own brands, and started exporting in 1950

observations.value: the only producer making wine in all three towns of the sherry triangle — Jerez de la Frontera, El Puerto de Santa Maria and Sanlucar de Barrameda; it also created the Almacenista range that gave the category its name in the export market
International Wine & Spirit Competition Best Spanish Winery 2011 and Best Sherry Producer in 2014 and 2016

observations.unit: year — founded by a group including the British wine writer Hugh Johnson, as a pioneer of the revival of Tokaji after the communist era
ha, of which 57ha lie in three First Growths; the house works the first-growth vineyards Mezes Maly, Nyulaszo, Szt Tamas and Betsek

observations.unit: year — Giulio Cocchi, a Tuscan pastry chef, opened as a distiller and sparkling-wine maker at Asti in 1891; the Bava family have run the house since 1978

observations.unit: year — the Stelios Kechris Domaine has made wine near Thessaloniki since 1911; the Kechribari retsina — "amber" in Greek — was first made in 1939

observations.unit: year — founded by Vittorio Zoppi and Filippo Antonelli to revive old family recipes of the Piedmontese tradition. observations.value: the Vermouth di Torino Bianco recipe dates to the 1940s-50s, inherited from the great-uncle of the firm's office manager Paola Rogai — Carlin of the Monferrato, who worked for FIAT in Turin and made wine and vermouth from the family vines
base wine of Piedmontese Trebbiano, Chardonnay and Cortese; wormwood, marjoram, sage, coriander and iris macerated together, liquorice handled separately

observations.unit: year — founded by Juan Antonio Ponce at Villanueva de la Jara in DO Manchuela, after he worked at the Cooperativa de Iniesta and then for [[Telmo Rodríguez]]. DEFECT: the corpus files the region as "Valencia"; Manchuela is in Castilla-La Mancha/Cuenca
ha of old vines, much of it certified organic — Bobal, Monastrell, Garnacha and the rare Moravia Agria for reds, Albilla de Manchuela for whites

observations.unit: year — founded by the Michelini brothers Gerardo, Matias and Juan Pablo, first vintage 2008, at Gualtallary outside Tupungato in the Uco Valley
ha on sand, stone and limestone at about 1,370m — the highest winery in Mendoza; Malbec, Pinot Noir, Sauvignon Blanc and others

observations.value: organic practice in the vineyard and indigenous yeasts only in the cellar
observations.unit: qualitative
ha across Mendoza — 90ha at Agrelo, 242ha at Alto Agrelo, 14ha at Maipu with vines over 80 years old, and 452ha in the upper Uco Valley near Tupungato at 1,340m

observations.unit: qualitative

year — the bodega at Arnedo in Rioja Oriental began in 1899 and is the historic seat of the Marques del Atrio group; the family's fourth and fifth generations run it. NOT the same house as Faustino of Oyon, a distinction already recorded in §13.6

observations.value: built on Tempranillo; runs an active wine-tourism programme with guided tours, tastings and courses at Arnedo
hillside vineyards below the Dolomites in Trentino — mountain air, mineral soils and wide diurnal range; the Pinot Grigio and Pinot Grigio Rosato are bottled as Vigneti delle Dolomiti IGT

observations.unit: year — the brothers Raymond and Paul Lillet, liqueur makers and wine merchants, founded Maison Lillet at Podensac south of Bordeaux in 1872; the aperitif itself followed in 1887

observations.value: 85% Bordeaux regional wine blended with 15% handcrafted fruit liqueurs — macerations of sweet and bitter orange peel, cinchona bark and guarded other ingredients
took hold in Britain in the 1930s and 40s; Ian Fleming wrote it into the Vesper in Casino Royale

observations.unit: year — Opia was created by Chavin (Pierre Chavin) as a French pioneer of alcohol-free wine; the wines are made at the Villa Noria domaine in the Languedoc

ALIAS: Prima Perla is a label of Cantina Montelliana, a Treviso cooperative founded in 1957 — the corpus string names the brand rather than the house
Glera from the hills of the Treviso province, soft-pressed and given its second fermentation by the Charmat/Martinotti method in pressurised autoclaves to keep the varietal aromatics

SEARCH EXHAUSTED: queries for a Prosecco DOC producer or brand owner named "Piccolo Sogno" return only restaurant wine lists and an unrelated Chicago restaurant of that name. Assessment: a private-label or restaurant-exclusive Prosecco whose maker is not disclosed — an identity that cannot be researched from public sources, which is a different thing from one not yet researched
ALIAS: the estate is Tenuta di Corte Giacobbe, part of Azienda Agricola Dal Cero Fratelli at Ronca in the province of Verona; the corpus drops "Corte"
